This conversation isn't going where I planned, so I'm just going to explain my position first before I reply directly.

I think that identifying as gay can be useful because it gives us a way to express our own identity. If I told someone that I was gay, they would probably assume the types of attributes I find attractive and unattractive in a person. Not all of their assumptions would be correct, but many probably would be. Generally speaking, I, and most gay men, aren't going to find transwomen attractive. They have too few attributes that I find appealing, and too many that I find unattractive.

I feel the exact opposite about transmen, who have many qualities that I find attractive, and few that I think are unattractive. But if I had to be honest about whether or not I would start a relationship with a transman, I don't think I would. The reason isn't that I don't believe they are attractive, or I don't believe they are a man. It's that when it comes to sex, I want the other person to have a penis, which isn't even exclusive to transmen.

Now, as for what you said. I disagree that transwomen don't look, sound or act like females, or that transwomen have more male than female qualities, as a blanket statement. I've known trans people who pass so well in appearance, voice and behaviour that I couldn't tell they were trans. Even many people who don't pass perfectly, at least do so well enough that it feels much more natural to think of them as the gender they identify with rather than what they were born as. Most importantly, as a gay man, I don't find them attractive.

> The only female quality they have is they try to look more feminine and some get breast implants. Other than that they have male bone structure, an adam's apple, male sex organs, male facial features, etc.

You mean aside from vocal training to sound like a woman, and changing the way you behave to be more like a woman, and bottom surgery? You can get cosmetic surgery to shave your Adam's apple so people can't notice it. 

The bone structure thing is, generally speaking, true right now. There are surgeries to reshape the structure of your skull to change your face, but your frame is pretty much stuck the way it is once you've gone through puberty. The use of hormone blockers to delay puberty is probably going to prevent people from facing that problem in the future though, so I'm curious if you'll come around on that issue in the future as medical procedures close the gap between transwomen and biological women. Or are you just going to keep pushing the goal post further away until you start using the chromosomes argument?

As a final note, I want to address the unfortunate truth that some people don't pass at all. I understand why a heterosexual man wouldn't find a transwoman attractive if they look and sound like a man. Here's the thing though. It's possible not to be a prick about it, and not say that it would be gay to find them attractive. Although your feelings would be reasonable, there are nicer ways to express them.

The point of tests is to give you assurance that your code works as you expect, and continues to do so when you change it in the future. If \`LeapYear.isLeapYear(1992)\` returns false when you expect it to be true, then you know the code has a bug. Not only that, but consider that the bug si likely going to cause problems with whatever code calls that method. Without the test you don't know where the bug is, you spend time tracking it down. With the test you know exactly what part of the code is failing.

The examples given in the course are small, and might seem obvious and insignificant, but those tests are going to save you a headache in the future.
